captures.note: The trip-back decision (the core tension) is uninformed: no signal of how much energy the return climb needs, so the first collapse reads as a sucker punch, not a gamble the player chose. Need a return-cost hint or low-lamp warning tied to depth.

Rock blocks say 'Your pickaxe is not strong enough' but no pickaxe upgrade exists anywhere; a player hits this dead end inside the first 10 seconds (scripted run stalled at depth 8 unable to descend). The message promises progression the game does not have.

One material (emerald) plus rare part cache: every dig is the same decision. Depth changes nothing visible (same dirt color, same loot density feel), so there is no pull to go deeper beyond abstract numbers.

Up-moves only work through already-dug cells and there is no way to dig upward, so a zigzag descent must be retraced from memory; the playtest run ended stranded at depth 4 with 3 emeralds it could not bank. Needs ladders, an escape consumable, or clearer tunnel breadcrumbs.

Zero dig feedback: blocks vanish instantly, the miner teleports cell to cell, no particles, crack states, or sound. The core action feels binary; even the rare part-cache find produces no fanfare beyond a HUD count.
No sense of descent: dirt is one flat color at every depth, no strata bands, no depth milestone markers, large black emptiness around the small grid. HUD says depth 10 but the world does not.
Mechanics base is solid: deterministic grid, energy and banking flow works, cash-out credits the wallet, zero console errors across the full scripted production run. The skeleton deserves the flesh.

Ore-tiers slice confirmed on production: scripted run dug to depth 14, the Entering Clay Beds banner fired over a visibly redder stratum, copper/silver/coal/cache all read as distinct block colors, the HUD showed carried value (2 coal worth 2 cr) and climb cost (~7.0 energy), and cash-out paid 2 cr + 15 cr first-reach depth bonus with zero console errors. F-012, F-014, F-017 confirmed fixed in production.
The /mine subtitle still reads 'dig for emeralds, find rare parts, make it back up'; emeralds are now one mid-tier ore and the currency is credits. Update the copy to match the ore-tier world.
